title: THEY ARE ALMOST READY TO STONE ME

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"Then Moses cried out to the LORD, 'What am I to do with these people? They are
almost ready to stone me.'" - Ex 17:4 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here is Moses, and he is not coping.

Look at what he does with it. He cries out to the LORD. And look at how he
speaks: "What am I to do with these people?" There is no polish here, no careful
religious phrasing. It is exasperation, spoken plainly to God.

God does not rebuke him for the tone. He answers with instructions.

This is one of the quiet mercies of Scripture. God's servants are allowed to be
at the end of themselves and to say so. Elijah sat under a tree and asked to die
(1 Kgs 19:4). Jeremiah told God He had deceived him (Jer 20:7). David asked how
long God would forget him (Ps 13:1).

None of these men were disciplined for honesty. God fed Elijah and let him
sleep.

If you are leading anything, a family, a class, a small group, a church, there
will be days when you have nothing left and the people you serve seem to be
against you. The right move is not to perform strength. It is to say to God
exactly what Moses said.

Notice also that Moses did not go to the people with his frustration. He went to
God with it. That order protects everyone.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Are you being honest with God about what you are carrying?
2. Do you take your frustration to God first, or to other people?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, I bring You my exhaustion and my frustration without dressing it up. Meet
me the way You met Moses. Amen.
